text:
srinivas: Quick share — zonal quantization bench for Marlin-7B (chat small-batch). GPUs: H100, A100, T4. Regions: us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1. Focus: batch=1-4 latency, throughput, PPL/EM quality delta, kernel choice effects (fused-attn vs split-kernel) and cold-start. TL;DR: INT8 gives ~1.9-2.6x token/sec speedup vs FP16 with ~0.3-0.9% PPL delta; FP8 shows 2.4-3.0x but higher variance on A100 eu-west due to kernel fallback. Full snippet below. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
eva: Nice. Can you paste the exact bench command and the summary CSV?
srinivas: Sure — ran with unified-kv enabled and warm cache runs (5 iters warm, 20 iters measure). Command:```bash ./bench_runner --model marlin-7b --profile {fp16,bf16,int8,fp8} --gpu ${GPU} --region ${REGION} --batch-sizes 1,2,4 --kernel {fused,split} --warm 5 --iters 20 --seq-len 512```Summary CSV header: gpu,region,profile,kernel,batch,median_latency_ms,median_tokens_per_sec,ppl_delta_percent
Here are a few rows (median across seeds):
H100,us-east-1,fp16,fused,1,42.3,480,0.0
H100,us-east-1,int8,fused,1,22.1,920,0.6
H100,us-east-1,fp8,fused,1,18.0,1120,0.9
A100,eu-west-1,fp16,split,1,58.5,350,0.0
A100,eu-west-1,int8,split,1,32.0,640,0.8
A100,eu-west-1,fp8,split,1,29.8,690,1.6  <-- note variance + kernel fallback logs showed nvcc warnings
T4,ap-southeast-1,fp16,split,1,120.5,160,0.0
T4,ap-southeast-1,int8,split,1,72.0,270,0.4
T4,ap-southeast-1,fp8,split,1,65.0,300,0.7
jonathan: That fp8 EM delta 1.6% on A100 is worrying. Was that due to quantization or kernel mismatch? Any logs?
srinivas: Root cause: A100 driver/kernel combo triggered a fallback path that duplicated some GEMM ops in float32 for numerical stability; seen as "kernel_fallback: true" in logs. When we forced the newer fused-attn kernel (cuda-profiler build), fp8 improved and variance reduced but required a newer CUDA toolkit that we don't ship to all zones yet. Attached small log excerpt:```[2026-02-12T14:03:22Z] kernel_fallback: true -- op matmul_12 fallback to fp32
[2026-02-12T14:03:22Z] kv_cache_hit: 0.96
[2026-02-12T14:03:23Z] fused_attn_used: false (split used)```
eva: For production chat (batch=1) cold-start matters. What's cold-start 95th latency on int8 vs fp16?
srinivas: Cold-start (first request after model load, measured on H100 us-east): fp16 p95=220ms, int8 p95=140ms, fp8 p95=125ms. Warm steady-state p99 (H100, batch=1): fp16=480ms token latency peak (this is per-token generation throughput converted), int8 reduces token-latency cost but watch quality. Note: our measurements convert per-token time to tokens/sec; end-to-end chat latency adds decoding overhead and network e2e.
maya: For sizing: target is 120 qps sustained (incoming chat requests) with 200ms tail latency budget for prompt+generation. How many GPUs?
srinivas: Quick calc (marlin-7b, average 40 tokens per response):
- H100 fused-int8: median tokens/sec ~920 -> responses/sec ~23 -> need 120/23 ~= 5.2 => 6 H100s per zone (reserve 20% headroom)
- A100 split-int8: median tokens/sec ~640 -> responses/sec ~16 -> need ~8 => recommend 10 A100s for eu-west (headroom + failover)
- T4 int8 (edge region): responses/sec ~6 -> need ~20 -> not cost-effective for this throughput
These are baseline; use autoscale burst for load spikes.
jonathan: Any config flags we should expose in Dedicated/Private that helped?
srinivas: Yes - recommend: "--kernel=fused" for H100 stacks, "--unified-kv=true" always, "--quant-drop-prob=0.01" (helps stability for int8 on long contexts) and an optional fallback policy: region_policy: prefer_fused -> fallback_split -> degrade_to_fp16. Also enable per-route quality monitoring comparing EM/PPL on rolling prompts.
bench-bot: New dashboard uploaded: https://redwood-internal/bench/marlin-7b/zonal-quant/1862123345 (contains full CSVs, raw logs, flamegraphs). :eyes:
eva: Action items?
maya: 1) Add a CI smoke that runs FP8 on A100 eu-west nightly with the newer fused kernel build (catch regressions). 2) Update capacity runbook with H100 sizing notes. 3) Flag drivers in eu-west that force fallback to be updated.
srinivas: I'll open the PR with the updated kernel flags + bench harness changes and attach logs. Also we'll add a short eval set for conversational quality to track the 0.x% deltas automatically.
jonathan: Thanks — please include a quick snippet to reproduce the perf/quality CSV for the release notes.
srinivas: Will do.```
